# Intent (advisory)
# zBuild — Vision
> The North Star for zBuild — it steers how zBuild is built. The README distills it; the wiki references it; every pipeline run is steered by it.
## Intent
zBuild turns a delivery process into data — templates and plugins — so software is built the same disciplined way every time. We build zBuild the way zBuild builds: a minimal core, with all behavior plugin-delivered and template-composed. A good change is small, aligned to the spec, proven by a test, and wired into the live path — never scaffolding that looks finished but does nothing.
## Principles
- **Target-agnostic by contract** — zBuild builds *any* repository, not itself; the engine and plugins never assume the target's language, layout, or that zBuild is the target. Target knowledge lives in data — templates, config, per-repo overrides — never in code.
- **Spec wins over drift** — KEEPERS, ARCHITECTURE, and the ADRs are the source of truth; when code disagrees, the code changes, not the spec.
- **Small engine, behavior at the edges** — keep the core tiny; add capability as plugins composed in templates, never by growing the engine.
- **Safety is structural** — all model-bound text passes one redaction chokepoint; state is atomic and resumable; scope is governed at every boundary.
- **Models are data, not code** — selection flows through the router and config tiers; never hardcode a model name.
- **Prove behavior, then wire it** — every change ships a test that fails without it and connects to the live path; green-but-inert is a defect.
- **Fail closed, never silent** — gates block on real problems and say why; bounded cycles and recovery drive work to done.
- **Dogfood every change** — build zBuild with zBuild; if the pipeline can't ship it, fix the pipeline.

# Plan: Exclude legacy/ from issue worktrees via sparse-checkout

**Goal:** Apply sparse-checkout to every issue worktree so legacy/ is absent (except legacy/migrated/), eliminating the ~50% tree overhead from every repo-wide agent search, without affecting the operator's main checkout.

## Steps
1. Write the regression test first (TDD). tests/unit/worktree-sparse-legacy-test.sh builds a real git repo with a legacy/ tree (including legacy/migrated/sentinel.md), calls zbuild_worktree_acquire and zbuild_worktree_enter, then asserts: (a) legacy/ content is absent except legacy/migrated/; (b) legacy/migrated/ files are present; (c) a branch switch inside the worktree retains the exclusion; (d) a second zbuild_worktree_acquire call (reuse path) retains the exclusion; (e) git -C <repo_root> config core.sparseCheckout is not 'true' in the main checkout after the operation. This test must fail (red) at the merge-base before any implementation change.
   - Files: `tests/unit/worktree-sparse-legacy-test.sh`
   - Estimated lines: 85
2. Add sparse-checkout support to scripts/lib/worktree.sh. (a) New internal helper _zbuild_worktree_apply_sparse <wt> <repo_root>: enables extensions.worktreeConfig=true on the main repo's .git/config (per-worktree isolation; does not change main checkout's sparsity), then runs 'git -C "$wt" sparse-checkout set --no-cone /* !/legacy/ /legacy/migrated/' inside the linked worktree. (b) New public function zbuild_worktree_include_legacy_path <wt> <path>: calls 'git -C "$wt" sparse-checkout add "$path"' to widen the sparse set for a keeper PR that must read or git-rm a specific legacy source. (c) Call _zbuild_worktree_apply_sparse at the reuse return (zbuild_worktree_acquire line ~182) and after the new-tree post-condition check (line ~203). (d) Call _zbuild_worktree_apply_sparse at the reuse return (zbuild_worktree_enter line ~242) and after the new-tree creation (line ~282).
   - Files: `scripts/lib/worktree.sh`
   - Estimated lines: 38
3. Amend ADR-059 §2 to record the sparse-checkout decision: add a paragraph under 'Why the worktree belongs to the issue' stating that legacy/ is excluded via per-worktree sparse-checkout (extensions.worktreeConfig) with legacy/migrated/ kept materialised, and that a run whose scope names a legacy/ path must call zbuild_worktree_include_legacy_path to widen the sparse set before operating on that path. Add the required '## Enforced by' section naming tests/unit/worktree-sparse-legacy-test.sh (new, §2 sparse exclusion), tests/unit/worktree-location-test.sh (§2 issue-keyed path shape, SPEC-9 through SPEC-11), and tests/unit/legacy-e1-tombstone-test.sh (§2 legacy/migrated/ intact). Then remove ADR-059-issue-vs-run-keying.md from config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt so lint-adr-enforced-by.sh stops exempting it.
   - Files: `docs/adr/ADR-059-issue-vs-run-keying.md`, `config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt`
   - Estimated lines: 18

## Notes
Sparse-checkout pattern rationale: '/*' includes everything by default; '!/legacy/' excludes the entire legacy tree; '/legacy/migrated/' re-includes only the tombstone subdirectory. This is a no-cone pattern (--no-cone) because the default cone mode would not correctly handle negation patterns. extensions.worktreeConfig must be set on the main repo before the per-worktree sparse-checkout file is written; without it, git writes a shared sparse-checkout file and ALL worktrees (including the operator's main checkout) become sparse. Setting extensions.worktreeConfig is safe and additive — it does not alter any existing checkout; it only enables per-WT config files going forward. The guard test for 'main checkout not made sparse' checks git -C repo_root config core.sparseCheckout and asserts it is absent or false. The keeper-PR widening function (zbuild_worktree_include_legacy_path) is explicitly requested by the issue ('say how') but is not yet called by any engine code — the call site is in the engine's scope-reading stage, which is out of scope for this issue. The function ships but the caller is a follow-up. Branch-switch retention: once sparse-checkout is set via worktreeConfig, it persists through git checkout calls inside the linked worktree — this is a property of git's sparse-checkout mechanism, not something zbuild needs to actively maintain. The test verifies it. ADR-002 is not amended here because the sparse-checkout decision is a worktree-materialisation property (§2 of ADR-059), not a change to the sentinel protocol or the pruning protocol that ADR-002 governs. The issue references 'ADR-002' only as context for the established legacy/ exclusion convention, not as the locus of the new statement.

### DESIGN DECISIONS (from the design stage — honor these directives; they refine the plan)
# Design: Exclude legacy/ from issue worktrees via sparse-checkout (#1802)

## Summary

**Goal:** Apply per-worktree sparse-checkout to every issue worktree so `legacy/` is absent (except `legacy/migrated/`), eliminating the ~50% tree overhead every repo-wide agent search currently pays.

**Context:** `legacy/` is a frozen, never-executed reference copy (~50% of the tree). Every agent running inside an issue worktree traverses it at full cost. ADR-059 §2 already notes that `legacy/` is materialised once per issue instead of once per run (#1802); this issue writes the mechanism that makes that note true.

**Decision:** Add `_zbuild_worktree_apply_sparse <wt> <repo_root>` to `scripts/lib/worktree.sh`. It sets `extensions.worktreeConfig=true` on the main repo config (enabling per-worktree isolation), then runs `git -C "$wt" sparse-checkout set --no-cone -- '/*' '!/legacy/' '/legacy/migrated/'` inside the linked worktree. Call it at every return point of both `zbuild_worktree_acquire` (new creation and reuse) and `zbuild_worktree_enter` (all three modes, new creation and reuse). Also ship `zbuild_worktree_include_legacy_path <wt> <path>` for keeper PRs that must read or `git rm` a specific legacy source before migration. Amend ADR-059 §2 to document the decision and add the required `## Enforced by` section; remove ADR-059 from `config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt`.

**Why `extensions.worktreeConfig`:** Without it, `git sparse-checkout set` writes `$repo/.git/info/sparse-checkout`, which is shared across all worktrees including the main checkout — making every linked worktree operation sparsify the operator's tree. `extensions.worktreeConfig=true` directs git to write `$repo/.git/worktrees/<name>/sparse-checkout` instead; the main checkout's sparsity is never touched.

**Pattern rationale:** `--no-cone` mode is required because cone mode cannot express negation patterns. The pattern `/* !/legacy/ /legacy/migrated/` includes everything by default, excludes the entire `legacy/` subtree, and re-includes `legacy/migrated/` so tombstones remain readable from within the worktree.

**Branch-switch retention:** Once sparse-checkout is set via `worktreeConfig`, it persists through `git checkout` calls inside the linked worktree. This is a property of git's mechanism, not something zBuild must actively maintain.
